A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the existence of an optimal $w$-matching machine, which is a finite state machine with the smallest asymptotic speed.

, for any given $w$-matching machine, we provide a method to compute the asymptotics of its speed, and conversely, we show that any algorithm with a given asymptotic speed can be simulated by some $w$-machines.

we have developed the theory of $w$-matching automata, we have proved that they characterize the asymptotic speed of pattern matching algorithms, and finally we have proved that the optimal asymptotic speed of a pattern $w$ is the inverse of the entropy of $w$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal speed of a pattern matching algorithm is given by the speed of the optimal $w$-matching machine for the same pattern $w$.
the asymptotic speed is a continuous function of $w$ and that it is possible to find an optimal pattern for any given machine, i.e. a pattern which maximizes the asymptotic speed.
, in general, the asymptotic speed is the same for all algorithms which use the same $w$-matching machine.
